doc.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Bobby Darin tribute CD with Elvin Jones and Thad Jones
summary: The Darin homage with Gary LeMel and Bobby Colomby, and Elvin Jones recalling Thad.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I measure my work by, did I do the very best that I could at the time. And this is definitely something that lives with me. I can play some of these charts and just go right back to stage and it’s the energy and the love and all, of making music together. And incidentally, as an aside, I just finished a CD which is a “Bobby Darin Homage” with Gary LeMel as the vocalist, president of Warner Brothers music, ex bass player, and Bobby Colomby of Blood Sweat and Tears is the producer and I’m the arranger. We had Elvin Jones, we had the Brecker Brothers, we had — Bobby Colomby, we were having lunch together and he said, “When was the last vocal album you ever saw Elvin Jones’ name on?” I said, “I’ve never.” He said, “Yeah, exactly. We’re going to use Elvin.” So we go to the Jazz Bakery and we meet Elvin. I hadn’t seen Elvin in 15 years. We played

something at the mayor’s house in New York years and years ago for George Wein or some party. And he said, “I’d love to do it.” In fact the first thing he said to me, which is one of the dearest things that anybody’s ever said to me, we were hugging and he whispered in my ear, “Thad always talked about you.” And it was just like wow.
I said oh man, how nice. Because I played with Thad’s Ball of Fire big band in Europe in ’83, we did a concert and a bunch of recordings, and he was part of “More Blues and the Abstract Truth.”
